title: How do we find the angles that are not marked?
description: A straight line and two rays from a point on it are drawn, with two angles marked. The marked angle is taken away from the straight angle, and again from the right angle, to find the two angles that are not marked. Keeko doubts that a straight angle is a full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: an unknown angle is the whole angle take away the known part, where the whole is a straight angle of one hundred eighty degrees or a right angle of ninety. Watch for students who use three hundred sixty for a straight angle.

source: In this figure, ∠TER = 80°. What is the measure of ∠BET? What is the measure of ∠SET?
video_script.why: The child sees that an unknown angle is the whole angle with the known part taken away.
video_script.substitution: Take the known 80 degrees away from the straight angle of 180 degrees, and again from the right angle of 90 degrees.
video_script.anchor: the book's figure: the straight line B R through E, with the rays E S and E T rising from E
video_script.wrong_answer: a straight angle is three hundred sixty degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a straight angle is three hundred sixty degrees. Three hundred sixty degrees is a full turn, and a straight angle is only half of it.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle B E T is one hundred degrees and the angle S E T is ten degrees

final_answer.spoken: the angle B E T is one hundred degrees and the angle S E T is ten degrees

maths_rules: ∠TER = 80° is part of ∠BER, and the rest is ∠BET
∠TER = 80° is part of ∠SER, and the rest is ∠SET
video_script.design: One figure: the straight line B R through E, the ray E T in teal, the ray E S in amber. The 80 degree part is shaded once and reused in both subtractions.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a straight line B R through the point E; the rays E S and E T rise from E; the angle T E R is marked 80° and the angle S E R is marked with a square corner and 90°

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.line: the straight line B R is drawn through E, and the rays E S and E T rise from E
marks.sizes: the angle T E R is marked 80° and the angle S E R 90°
marks.ask: question marks glow on the angles B E T and S E T

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about angles at the point E.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The line B R is straight.
Two more rays, E S and E T, rise from E.
<bookmark mark='sizes'/>The angle T E R is eighty degrees.
The angle S E R is ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What do the angles B E T and S E T measure?

beats.on_screen: the figure holds still on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the figure again: the angle B E R along the straight line is shaded and labelled straight angle 180°; the angle S E R is labelled right angle 90°; the 80° part is shaded inside each of them

marks.line: the angle B E R along the straight line is shaded and labelled straight angle 180°
marks.right: the angle S E R is labelled right angle 90°
marks.part: the 80° part is shaded inside each of the two bigger angles

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>The angle B E R lies along a straight line, so it is a straight angle.
A straight angle is one hundred eighty degrees, a half turn.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The angle S E R is a right angle of ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='part'/>The angle T E R sits inside both, so it is one part of each.

beats.on_screen: Given: ∠TER = 80°, ∠SER = 90°, B E R is a straight line

marks.given: the two measures and the straight line are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the angle T E R is eighty degrees.
The angle S E R is ninety degrees.

marks.find: the two angles to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the angle B E T and the angle S E T.

marks.whole: the straight angle 180° is written, with the 80° part shaded teal
marks.rest: 80° is taken away from 180° and the amber part is left

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step one, the straight angle B E R is one hundred eighty degrees.
The angle T E R covers eighty of it.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Take away eighty from one hundred eighty, because the rest is the angle B E T.

marks.whole: the right angle 90° is written, with the 80° part shaded teal
marks.rest: 80° is taken away from 90° and the amber part is left

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step two, the right angle S E R is ninety degrees.
The angle T E R covers eighty of it.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Take away eighty from ninety, because the rest is the angle S E T.

marks.ans: the two answers are boxed on the amber parts

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The angle B E T is one hundred degrees and the angle S E T is ten degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the figure
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says a straight angle is 360° and is then crossed out; a full circle is drawn beside the half circle; the full circle is labelled full turn and the half circle is labelled half of it

marks.full: a full circle is drawn beside the half circle and labelled full turn
marks.half: the half circle is labelled half of it, and the bubble is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a straight angle is three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='full'/>But three hundred sixty degrees is a full turn, a whole circle.
<bookmark mark='half'/>A straight angle is only half of that, so it is one hundred eighty degrees.
